notes: Game structure for mechanic analysis. artifacts = the wiki's master table on the 'Artifact' page; owner is crew / ship / common / boss / special (owner_name = crew member or ship; 'boss' = generic boss artifact, crew- or ship-specific boss artifacts keep owner crew/ship with rarity 'Boss'; 'special' = Hardmode, event, Cleo and Finale artifacts). events = the Events page table (zones, prerequisites) + each event page's Options list, plus the special Boot Sequence. ships = pages using Template:Ship. rules = sentences and lists lifted from Locations, Common Enemy/Elite/Boss, Repair Yard, Hardmode, Hull, Boot Sequence, Characters, Starting Deck, Achievements, Mechanics, Ship Parts, Finale and Patch 1.1/1.2; gaps are listed where the wiki is silent (node counts, memory unlock rules).

discrepancies: Main Page blurb says '80 artifacts' but the master table has 93 (stale blurb, Patch 1.0.6 / 1.1 added artifacts)
in Events table but not in Category:Events: ['Garbage Girl Repairs'] (page lacks the category tag)
Events page: Codex counts 23 events, 22 unique (Fake Distress Signal has a Drake variant); table rows = 22

events.name: Exploded Ships
events.intro: Exploded Ships is an event during which your ship stumbles upon a minefield full of exploded ships that you might be able to find cool stuff in! This event can appear in Zone 1, Zone 2, or Zone 3.
events.summary: Grab the first thing you can find! -> Lose 1 HP, Gain 1 Artifact | Let's look around for a bit. -> Lose 3 HP, Gain 1 of 4 Artifacts (Hard+: 1 of 3) | It's not worth it. Let's go.

events.name: Extra-Planar Being
events.intro: Extra-Planar Being is an event during which the crew is given a boon by an unknown entity in the area that matters most to them. This event can appear in Zone 1, Zone 2, or Zone 3.
events.summary: Healing. -> Add a card: Ephemeral Repairs | Damage. -> Add a card: Ephemeral Blast | Evasion. -> Add a card: Ephemeral Dodge

events.name: Ship Shuffler
events.intro: Ship Shuffler is an event at the Sunshine Heavy Industries ship yard, in which Selene tries to convince you to shuffle the order of your ship parts. This event can appear in Zone 1, Zone 2, or Zone 3.
events.summary: Shuffle me! -> Shuffle your ship parts and gain +2 max hull (Hard+: +1 max hull) | Absolutely not.

events.name: Garbage Girl Repairs
events.intro: Garbage Girl Repairs is an event during which you are offered a choice of hull repair options by Garbage Girl: either a normal repair or an "extra spicy" one. This event can appear in Zone 1, Zone 2, or Zone 3, but only if your ship's current hull is below 70% of its max.
events.summary: Extra spicy!!! -> Gain Scrap Armor | Uh, regular please. -> Heal 50% hull

events.name: Grandma's Bakery and Weapons Market
events.intro: Grandma's Bakery and Weapons Market is an event during which you visit Grandma's store to gain a rare card, remove a card, or (presumably) just pick up a few pastries for the road. This event can appear in Zone 1, Zone 2, or Zone 3.
events.summary: One treat please! -> Gain 1 random upgraded rare card (Hard+: non-upgraded) | Can we use your trash can? -> Remove a card from your deck || Notes: Note that there is no skip option for this event.

events.name: High-Pitched Static
events.intro: High-Pitched Static is an event during which a mysterious entity offers to teach you, potentially gifting you with a card from a present crew member. This event can appear in Zone 1, Zone 2, or Zone 3.
events.summary: Obtain one of 3 [1st crewmember] cards. (Hard+: 1 of 2) | Obtain one of 3 [2nd crewmember] cards. (Hard+: 1 of 2) | Obtain one of 3 [3rd crewmember] cards. (Hard+: 1 of 2) | I don't trust this! || Notes: Note that if you choose to take a card offering here, you must pick a card and cannot skip it.

events.name: Abandoned Shipyard
events.intro: Abandoned Shipyard is an event that involves finding an abandoned ship yard that can be used to patch the hull but there was a mysterious signal. This event can only appear in Zone 1, but only if your ship's current hull below 70% of its max.
events.summary: Try to repair the ship -> 50% success chance (Hard+: 33% success chance): Heal 50% hull.; 50% failure chance (Hard+: 67% failure chance): Heal 1 hull and enter combat with CCD-62 "Cicada" Drone Mk2. | Let's keep moving.

events.name: Artifact Smuggling
events.intro: Artifact Smuggling is an event during which Brimford asks your crew to hold on to some contraband goods for a moment. Hopefully nobody notices… This event can appear in Zone 1.
events.summary: Sure! -> Gain random Artifact; 50% chance (Hard+: 75% chance): Enter combat with STG-04 "Stag" Fighter | Nah.

events.name: Fake Distress Signal
events.intro: Fake Distress Signal is an event during which you are accosted by Drake (or, if Drake is a part of the crew at the time, Drakebot 2) as she attempts to steal one of your artifacts. This event can only appear in Zone 1.
events.summary: Give her [random Artifact]. -> Lose the randomly chosen Artifact | Uh, no??? (With Drake in your crew, this changes to: Over my dead body!!!) -> Enter Combat with Fireball | We.. don't have any? -> Enter Combat with Fireball || Notes: If you have no artifacts, the following is your only option:

events.name: Welcome Back, Commander
events.intro: Welcome Back, Commander is an Event where you are hailed by an unmanned ship, whose malfunctioning AI falsely recognizes you as its commander and offers to upgrade your cards. This event only appears in Zone 1.
events.summary: 2 random cards gain upgrade A | 2 random cards gain upgrade B | Choose a card to upgrade || Notes: X.00 approaches you and offers one of the following options for upgrades.

events.name: Extra Scaffold
events.intro: Extra Scaffold is an Event at the Sunshine Heavy Industries shipyard during which Selene tries to convince you to add an empty scaffold to your ship. This event can appear in Zone 1 or Zone 2.
events.summary: Sure! -> If ship parts are currently even: Add an unshootable scaffold in the middle of the ship; If ship parts are currently odd: Add an unshootable scaffold to the right of the middle ship part | No thanks. || Notes: Selene asks if you want to add a piece of scaffolding right in the middle of your ship. You may choose to take the offer or not.

events.name: Missile Mayhem
events.intro: Missile Mayhem is an Event during which you are hailed by a frantic frog whose missiles have turned against him. Upon deciding to help, you enter combat against Soggin's Very Cool Ship, a Missiler class ship with the Missile Malfunction debuff.
events.summary: Help the toad. -> Enter.. combat? | Do not help. | This hard drive I found earlier! -> Gain Missile Malware | My precious seeker missiles! -> Gain Seeker | An artifact I found! -> Gain a random Common artifact. | Nevermind. || Notes: If you choose to help Soggins, you must prevent him from dying to his own missiles for 5 turns (Hard+: 6 turns). If you succeed, you get to pick a reward!

events.name: Sports!
events.intro: Sports! is an Event resembling a Football game (Soccer in North America), with you and an opponent ship fighting over the midrow Football. The event can be won either by shifting the Football to the left goal, or by destroying the opponent ship.
events.summary: Sure, why not. -> Enter Combat with Glorious Sport Arena | We're kind of busy right now. | Got any trophies? -> Gain 1 of 3 Artifacts | We'll take the ball. -> Gain Sport Orb | Can we have the ball? -> Gain Sport Orb | No thanks.

events.name: Upcycling Program
events.intro: Upcycling Program is another event that takes place at the Sunshine Heavy Industries shipyard. This time, Wren offers the crew an opportunity to "upcycle" a card in the deck by replacing it with a random better card, or maybe to "sidecycle" a card to a different deck instead.
events.summary: Replace a card with a random rarer card -> If the card belonged to one of your crewmembers, the new card will be from the same deck. Otherwise, it will be from a random crewmember on your ship.; Always goes up one step in rarity. (Common becomes Uncommon, Uncommon becomes Rare); Rare cards cannot be chosen. | Replace a card with a same-rarity card from another deck -> The new card will be from a different crewmember on your ship. | No thanks!

events.name: Crystallized Crew
events.intro: Crystallized Crew is an Event during which you stumble upon one of the other Characters, stuck inside of a crystal. You are given the option to save them at the cost of putting one of your current crew members back into stasis.
events.summary: Replace [crewmember 1] with [crystallized character] | Replace [crewmember 2] with [crystallized character] | Replace [crewmember 3] with [crystallized character] | They'll be fine. || Notes: The frozen character may be any of the other characters that you've unlocked, picked at random. You'll still keep the cards and artifacts of the crewmember you remove, if you choose to do so.

events.name: Your Old Friend Dracula
events.intro: Your Old Friend Dracula is an event during which your old pal, Dracula, spends some time catching up with the crew and offering to teach them some dark vampire arts. This event can only appear in Zone 2.
events.summary: Just a little. -> Gain Leech | Ok, I'll take a lot. -> Gain two Leeches, but lose 30% hull (Hard+: 60% hull) | No thanks, Dracula!

events.name: Black Hole
events.intro: Black Hole is a negative Event where the crew jumps way too close to a black hole, resulting in a tough choice: jettison a possibly valuable card or lose a large chunk of the hull! This event can appear in Zone 2 or Zone 3.
events.summary: Lose [randomly chosen card from crewmember 1] | Lose [randomly chosen card from crewmember 2] | Lose [randomly chosen card from crewmember 3] | Jettison part of the hull! -> Lose half of your current hull (damage is rounded down)

events.name: Emporium of Wonderful Ideas
events.intro: Emporium of Wonderful Ideas is an Event that allows you to choose a "useless" card from a shop full of… questionable ideas. This event can appear in Zone 2 or Zone 3.
events.summary: Let's try Buckshot. -> Add a card: Buckshot | Give me Waltz. -> Add a card: Waltz | How about Bruise? -> Add a card: Bruise | Lightning in a Bottle, please! -> Add a card: Lightning in a Bottle | Yeah, no. || Notes: You may choose one of the cards below to add to your deck, or decline the offer. (Hard+: one of the card options is removed at random)

events.name: Offering from Another Timeline
events.intro: Offering from Another Timeline is an event during which a mysterious entity offers aid from an alternate timeline, potentially gifting you with a card from a not-present crew member. This event can appear in Zone 2 or Zone 3, but only if Isaac is unlocked.
events.summary: Take one of 3 [random non-crewmember] cards (Hard+: 1 of 2) | Take one of 3 [random non-crewmember] cards (Hard+: 1 of 2) | Take one of 3 [random non-crewmember] cards (Hard+: 1 of 2) | No thanks. || Notes: The 3 decks you can choose from are picked randomly, from characters that aren't in your crew. Note that if you have less than 6 characters unlocked in total, then only one or two options will be present.

events.name: The Duplitron
events.intro: The Duplitron is an Event during which you may submit to testing Dr. Bjorn's new device: the Duplitron!
events.summary: Duplicate a card in your deck. | Duplicate a card in your deck four times. Lose 3 max hull. (Hard+: lose 4 max hull) | Mmm.. no thanks.

events.name: Worthwhile Trade Repairs
events.intro: Worthwhile Trade Repairs is an event that features a slug that offers you repairs for a price. This event can appear in Zone 2 or Zone 3, but only if your ship's current hull below 70% of max.
events.summary: Trade away [random Artifact]. Gain 5 max hull (Hard+: 3 max hull) and heal to full. | No thanks.

events.name: Annoying Debate
events.intro: Annoying Debate is an Event in which you may join Brimford for a bit of debate to swap some of your card upgrades. This event can only appear in Zone 3.
events.summary: Turn an Upgrade A card into a B. Gain an Annoyance. (Hard+: Gain an Annoyance A) | Turn an Upgrade B card into an A. Gain an Annoyance. (Hard+: Gain an Annoyance A) | No, thanks. || Notes: Choosing to swap an upgrade will let you make another choice afterwards, and you can keep going infinitely until you decide to stop.

events.name: Boot Sequence
events.sector: Start of every loop after the first (special, always occurs)
events.intro: Boot Sequence is a special Event that always occurs at the start of every loop after your very first. It lets you choose from a variety of random bonuses, and if you're playing on the Hardest difficulty, forces you to pick a downside as well.
events.summary: Gain 3 max hull | Gain 1 common artifact | Replace Warp Prep with a boss artifact | Remove 2 cards | Remove a card, then gain 1 of 3 common cards | Pick from 3 uncommon cards | Gain 1 random rare card | Upgrade a card | Upgrade 2 random cards to type A | Upgrade 2 random cards to type B | Gain 1 Debris | Lose 1 max shield | Lose 2 max hull || Notes: You may choose 1 of 3 bonuses picked randomly out of the following list: On Hardest, you must also choose one of the following downsides first, before you can choose a bonus:

ships.name: Ares
ships.description: A nimble warship with two cannons, which are manually toggled.
ships.summary: Ares is an unlockable Ship. Ares is four tiles wide and starts with Warp Prep, Ares Cannon, and Control Rods.

node_types.name: Common Enemy
node_types.summary: A basic enemy encounter with a reward of a choice of cards.
node_types.details: Common Enemies are the most common form of encounter in Cobalt Core. All Common Enemy encounters begin a battle with a hostile ship, and defeating them will always result in a card reward after the battle. The specific enemies encountered vary by zone, as shown below.

node_types.name: Elite
node_types.summary: An unusually strong enemy encounter with card and artifact rewards.
node_types.details: Elites are a challenging combat encounter with greater perils and greater rewards. All Elite encounters begin a difficult battle with a hostile ship, and defeating them will always result in both a card reward (with increased chances for Uncommon and Rare cards) and a choice of 3 artifacts (2 on Harder+) after the battle. Elite encounters vary by zone, as shown below. A given Elite can only be encountered at an Elite node once per zone, and map generation will ensure you cannot encounter more Elites than the zone has.

node_types.name: Boss
node_types.summary: A very powerful entity with substantial rewards.
node_types.details: Bosses are very challenging combat encounters at the end of each zone. All Boss encounters begin a very difficult battle with a hostile ship, and defeating them will always result in both an improved card reward and a Boss artifact reward after the battle. Boss encounters vary by zone, as shown below.

node_types.name: Event
node_types.summary: An unknown energy signature that offers a choice.
node_types.details: Events, marked on the map as "unknown energy signatures," contain story-based, optional choices as you progress through the loop. With few exceptions, events have positive outcomes for the player and are, at worst, skippable. There are 23 total Events in the Codex, but only 22 are unique, since one event has two variations that are counted separately in the Codex. Some events are locked to a particular Zone, while others have prerequisites, such as missing a certain percentage of Hull. Each event can only trigger once per loop, so you won't come across the same event multiple times.

node_types.name: Artifact
node_types.summary: An artifact to benefit the crew and change the rules of combat. You will receive one at random, unless you have the Artemis's Cargo Hold in which case you will be given a choice of two.
node_types.details: Artifacts are permanent items that provide passive bonuses during the loop. About half of the artifacts are available during every loop, with the other half being restricted to specific characters or ships. Artifacts can only be lost through certain Events. You cannot be offered artifacts you already have, but you can be offered artifacts you have seen previously on this run that you didn't take. You can even be offered artifacts that you previously had but lost. Each ship begins the loop with the Warp Prep artifact, and all ships also begin with one or more additional starting artifacts. Boss artifacts can only be found as rewards after a boss battle (or traded for Warp Prep during the Boot Option start-of-loop event). A select few artifacts require special circumstances, such as a specific Events choice, in order to be acquired.

node_types.name: Repair Yard
node_types.summary: A shop for ship repairs, card upgrades, and trash disposal.
node_types.details: Repair Yards are a type of Location you will see often on the map, denoted by their unique icon with a green wrench & screwdriver. Each zone has two Repair Yards scattered randomly throughout the middle and one just before the Boss which you are guaranteed to stop by. Because of the randomly diverging pathways, you will sometimes be unable to visit all 3 Repair Yards in a zone. At each Repair Yard, you will find Cleo, a friendly cat who is happy to help you on your journey.

node_types.name: Exit
node_types.summary: The exit from this zone and the entrance to the next!

map_structure: Visiting locations forms the primary gameplay loop of Cobalt Core. Each location may contain some combination of battle, player choice, or reward. Encounters at each location generally vary based on the current zone. Broad descriptions of every available location are listed below.
Because of the randomly diverging pathways, you will sometimes be unable to visit all 3 Repair Yards in a zone.

Three zones in order: Lazuli Nebula (1) -> Sapphire Cluster (2) -> Void's Cradle (3); each ends at a Boss, then an Exit node leads to the next zone (Locations table). The Finale is a separate battle launched from the Memories screen.

time_loop.boot_sequence: Boot Sequence is a special Event that always occurs at the start of every loop after your very first. It lets you choose from a variety of random bonuses, and if you're playing on the Hardest difficulty, forces you to pick a downside as well.

Remove a card, then gain 1 of 3 common cards

time_loop.memories_and_finale: The Finale is a special battle, accessible from the Memories screen after recovering all 18 Memories, in which CAT pilots The Cobalt to save her friends and end the loops. It is deliberately tilted in the player's favor, and if you do manage to lose (such as by deliberately skipping turns) you will instantly restart. Completing the Finale plays the credits. Completing it for the first time unlocks CAT for normal play.

overview: Combat in Cobalt Core boils down to strategic positioning.
There are three rows of parallel one-dimensional grids: Player row, Midrow, Enemy row.
Evasion is a mechanic that allows players and enemies to move along their respective row.
Players utilize a status effect called Evade, which acts like a consumable resource for movement.
Using 1 evade to move a unit left or right across the grid of their row.
Enemies, however, have set behaviors for evading.
See each enemy's unique behavior on their respective page.
Some enemies have set behaviors that allow them to instantly move to line up the center of their ship to the center of the player's ship.

This happens if the player's footprint ceases from being aligned to am enemy's ship part, in which they will "square up." Hull is the main health attribute that the player wants to protect on their ship, and deplete on the enemy ship.
If Hull falls below 0, the respective ship is destroyed, and in the player's case, game over.
Shield is the secondary health attribute that a ship can raise to protect the Hull.
Shield acts as extra hitpoints that takes damage before the Hull.
Since Shield is easier to come by than healing, it is an important resource to mitigating Hull damage.
Players and enemies can both raise shields, but the player has ways of ignoring the enemy's shield with Piercing attacks.

ship_parts.Cockpit: The cockpit is where the pilot(s) are, probably. All player ships have a cockpit. Most enemy ships also have a cockpit, but there are some that don't. On Hard difficulty or above, the player's cockpit will be Weak by default, meaning it will take +1 damage from all attacks.
ship_parts.Cannon: The cannon is where all attacks come out of, usually. All player ships have one cannon, with some exceptions. The Ares and Gemini both have two separate cannons which they can switch between. The Jupiter has no cannons and instead channels its attacks through Jupiter Drones.
ship_parts.Missile Bay: The missile bay is where midrow objects such as missiles & drones are launched from. All player ships have one missile bay, except for the Gemini which has two missile bays that it can switch between. Some enemy ships also have missile bays. When the player launches an object, it is released into the midrow on the same lane as their missile bay.
ship_parts.Comms: Comms is a part only seen on the Jupiter ship. It is Weak by default, regardless of difficulty. Other than that, it has no innate effects or properties. With the Radar Subwoofer artifact (exclusive to the Jupiter), the Comms will boost the attack of any Jupiter Drone in front of it by +1.
ship_parts.Wings: The wings probably help make ships move better, although they aren't necessary parts on all ships and don't have any impact on gameplay by themselves. Of the player-controlled ships, the Artemis, Jupiter and Tiderunner are the only ones to have wings. Many enemy ships also have wings. With the Hunter Wings boss artifact (exclusive to the Artemis), the player's wings can temporarily become Empty if they end their turn with 1 or more Energy.
ship_parts.Empty Parts: Some ships will have empty scaffolding in the middle of them, where attacks and missiles will pass right through them as if there was nothing there. They still act as a part of the ship otherwise. The only player-controlled ships to start with Empty parts are the Jupiter and the Tiderunner. Some enemy ships also have Empty parts.
